answer: Velvet draw slots. Each epoch, a verifiable random function assigns identities to scarce task slots; assignment needs a valid VRF proof bound to a fresh, unconsumed seed the network publishes only at epoch open. An attacker cannot precompute which identities land where, so bulk registration yields no scheduling advantage. Saffron weighting makes unassigned identities decay, forcing continuous activity cost. Maintaining a large dormant swarm through many epochs becomes the price, since each identity must hold a live haven and pay renewal, and the randomness denies any predictive edge.
